newsitem.title: DUBAI: U.S. business, officials in Saudi for trade talks.
newsitem.headline: U.S. business, officials in Saudi for trade talks.

text.p: U.S. businessmen arrived in Saudi Arabia on Tuesday to discuss ways to boost trade and technology transfers in joint projects, while a U.S.-Gulf economic dialogue opened in Riyadh, officials said.
The two-day businessmen's meeting, organised by the Washington-based Arab American National Chamber, will also detail Saudi investment incentives to lure foreign investors.
The delegation will meet government officials as well as members of the Saudi Arabian chambers of commerce and industry.
The United States-Gulf Cooperation Council economic dialogue is aiming to boost trade links, the GCC said in a statement.
U.S. Commerce Department counsellor Jan Kalicki is leading the U.S. side in the twice a year talks which will focus on investment and dual taxation exemptions.
Total U.S. trade with the six GCC states grew 16 percent last year to almost $25 billion, Kalicki has said.
Trade between the United States and its biggest commercial partner in the Middle East, Saudi Arabia, grew 12 percent last year to $16.7 billion.
U.S. companies had invested over $6.7 billion in Saudi Arabia up until the end of 1996 -- representing over 46 percent of total foreign investment in the kingdom.
The GCC, an economic and political alliance, is made up of Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Bahrain, Oman, UAE and Qatar.
